hook: Lukasz Kaiser earned a master's degree from the University of Wroclaw in Poland and a PhD from RWTH Aachen University in Germany in 2008, working on logic and automata theory. He then spent time as a tenured researcher at Paris Diderot University before joining Google Brain in 2013. There he helped build the TensorFlow system and later co-created the Tensor2Tensor and Trax libraries used for sequence modeling research. In 2017 he co-authored Attention Is All You Need, contributing to the Transformer architecture that reshaped natural language processing. He later moved to OpenAI, where he worked as a research scientist and was credited as the long context lead on the GPT-4 project, helping extend how much text the model could take into account at once.
